---
title: "How do I make a bar chart with readable category labels and counts?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I make a bar chart with readable category labels and counts?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Count categories with table().

2. Call barplot() and capture bar-center positions.

3. Use text() to show values above the bars.

## Runnable example

```{r}
responses <- c("bus","bike","bus","walk","walk","bus","bike")
counts <- table(responses)
at <- barplot(counts,col=c("#CDE1EF","#EAC99E","#B7D7C5"),
              border="#244967",ylab="Responses",
              main="Travel choices",ylim=c(0,max(counts)+2))
text(at,counts,labels=counts,pos=3)
```

## Interpret the result

Each bar represents a named category and its number of responses. The values above the bars prevent readers from estimating counts by eye.

## Check before applying to real data

Explain whether the bars show counts or percentages and include an appropriate zero baseline.
